00-01-why-this-history.md.commons: Berkey and Gay Furniture Company Factory -1.jpg
00-01-why-this-history.md.alt: Historic Berkey and Gay furniture factory in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where American casegoods manufacturing shaped retail showrooms
00-01-why-this-history.md.figcaption: Grand Rapids factories such as Berkey and Gay trained buyers to expect finished rooms and reliable lines long before online catalogs.

00-02-who-is-talking.md.commons: Woodworking for beginners; a manual for amateurs (1900) (14760550006).jpg
00-02-who-is-talking.md.alt: 1900 amateur woodworking manual illustration of bench tools and hand-cut joinery
00-02-who-is-talking.md.figcaption: This series speaks from a working bench—labor, lead time, and repeatability—not from a marketplace dashboard.

00-03-four-doors.md.alt: Marshall Field and Company department store building on Chicago State Street, an early curated furniture retail door
00-03-four-doors.md.figcaption: Department stores were a fourth kind of door: edited rooms, trained buyers, and freight networks custom shops still inherit.

00-04-stolen-words.md.alt: Weathered handmade shop sign on a craft retail stall in Dingle, County Kerry, Ireland
00-04-stolen-words.md.figcaption: Words like handmade and artisan once pointed at visible labor; retail copy now often uses them as mood lighting.

01-05-america-house.md.commons: Museum of Arts and Design (MAD) - NYC (51395616531).jpg
01-05-america-house.md.alt: Museum of Arts and Design at Columbus Circle, New York, successor to the Museum of Contemporary Crafts era
01-05-america-house.md.figcaption: America House and the Museum of Contemporary Crafts shared Aileen Osborn Webb’s impulse to teach craft and sell it in the same city.

01-06-acc-fairs.md.alt: Juried outdoor craft fair booth displaying handmade goods to passing buyers
01-06-acc-fairs.md.figcaption: ACC-era fairs turned handmade furniture retail into a portable city: booth fees, juries, and buyers with checks or wholesale orders.

01-07-gallery-consignment.md.alt: Furniture store interior with displayed seating and casegoods arranged for browsing
01-07-gallery-consignment.md.figcaption: Consignment galleries sell access to a taught buyer; the split pays rent, editing, and the person who stays in the room.

01-08-studio-furniture-as-art.md.commons: Wharton Esherick House & Studio, 1520 Horsehoe Trail, Malvern (Chester County, Pennsylvania).jpg
01-08-studio-furniture-as-art.md.alt: Wharton Esherick House and Studio in Malvern, Pennsylvania, a landmark of American studio furniture
01-08-studio-furniture-as-art.md.figcaption: Studio furniture makers such as Wharton Esherick blurred the line between usable tables and museum objects.

01-09-table-as-bad-gallery-object.md.alt: Frank Lloyd Wright dining table on display, furniture meant for daily meals rather than pedestal isolation
01-09-table-as-bad-gallery-object.md.figcaption: A dining table is a bad gallery object: it wants a house, not a white cube and a price tag on the wall.

01-10-jury-and-booth.md.commons: Display of handmade pottery and wooden items in a craft market.jpg
01-10-jury-and-booth.md.alt: Handmade pottery and wooden craft items displayed at an outdoor market booth
01-10-jury-and-booth.md.figcaption: Fair juries and booth fees decide who gets a weekend door to metropolitan buyers.

01-11-what-galleries-taught.md.alt: Handmade pottery arranged on shelves in a small art gallery retail space
01-11-what-galleries-taught.md.figcaption: Galleries taught slow looking: spacing, light, and a person willing to explain why one bowl costs more.

01-12-gallery-to-showroom-handoff.md.commons: Character and individuality in decorations and furnishings. (1913) (14763841252).jpg
01-12-gallery-to-showroom-handoff.md.alt: 1913 interior design plate showing furnished rooms with coordinated decorations and furniture
01-12-gallery-to-showroom-handoff.md.figcaption: The handoff from gallery to trade showroom trades the single object for lines, samples, and designer relationships.

02-13-to-the-trade.md.commons: Character and individuality in decorations and furnishings. (1913) (14784034873).jpg
02-13-to-the-trade.md.alt: 1913 trade interior illustration of a decorated room set for professional specification
02-13-to-the-trade.md.figcaption: To-the-trade showrooms sell through designers; the public price list is often a different document.

02-14-design-centers.md.alt: Merchandise Mart along the Chicago River, a major wholesale design and furniture trade center
02-14-design-centers.md.figcaption: Design centers such as Chicago’s Merchandise Mart concentrate wholesale showrooms the way cities concentrate banks.

02-15-getting-the-line-in.md.alt: Wood stain finish samples laid out for furniture specification and showroom approval
02-15-getting-the-line-in.md.figcaption: Getting a line into a showroom starts with proof: samples, lead times, and photographs that match what the shop can build.

02-16-territory-exclusivity.md.commons: Main Floor plan - Nims Ford Dealership, 116 North Main Street, Ekalaka, Carter County, MT HABS MT-115 (sheet 3 of 8).tif
02-16-territory-exclusivity.md.alt: Historic main-floor plan diagram zoning a retail showroom into distinct sales territories
02-16-territory-exclusivity.md.figcaption: Territory exclusivity maps a city to one showroom; the map only works if the room is actually selling.

02-17-net-list-multiplier.md.commons: Retail price list of California bulbs (16375013340).jpg
02-17-net-list-multiplier.md.alt: Vintage printed retail price list with tiered numbers, a paper ancestor of trade net and list pricing
02-17-net-list-multiplier.md.figcaption: Net, list, and designer multipliers are how trade showrooms hide public price from casual browsers.

02-18-sample-floor.md.commons: Zemplín Museum in Michalovce - History permanent exhibition - Dining room - Overall view of the displayed 1910-1930 dining room furniture 01.jpg
02-18-sample-floor.md.alt: Museum dining room furniture vignette with table and chairs arranged as a walk-around sample floor
02-18-sample-floor.md.figcaption: A sample floor lets designers and clients believe a custom table before it exists in their room.

02-19-paper-trail.md.commons: Sears Wonder Book of Values, 1941 - Advertising Postcard (4342725077).jpg
02-19-paper-trail.md.alt: 1941 Sears advertising postcard promoting mailed retail values, part of the paper trail behind furniture orders
02-19-paper-trail.md.figcaption: Showroom orders still ride on paper trails: acknowledgements, deposits, and change orders with signatures.

02-20-cold-calling-designers.md.alt: Vintage rotary telephone on a desk, the tool behind cold-calling interior designers before CRM software
02-20-cold-calling-designers.md.figcaption: Cold-calling designers was the pre-internet CRM: a voice, two photographs, and a promise you could keep.

02-21-own-trucks.md.alt: 1911 advertisement for a furniture and household goods delivery moving company truck service
02-21-own-trucks.md.figcaption: Owning delivery trucks keeps the last mile in the shop’s hands when freight brokers treat a table like a carton.

03-22-high-point.md.commons: Southern Furniture Exhibition Building (High Point, North Carolina).jpg
03-22-high-point.md.alt: Southern Furniture Exhibition Building in High Point, North Carolina, hub of the wholesale furniture market
03-22-high-point.md.figcaption: High Point’s Southern Furniture Market dates to March 1909; twice a year the town becomes a wholesale city.

03-23-market-order-vs-cart.md.alt: 1897 wholesale price list page with line items and quantities for market buyers
03-23-market-order-vs-cart.md.figcaption: A market order assigns title and lead time; an e-commerce cart is a thinner promise with fewer signatures.

03-24-tear-sheets.md.commons: Santa Claus in a 1920 furniture ad.jpg
03-24-tear-sheets.md.alt: 1920s furniture advertisement with Santa Claus, an era when tear sheets sold rooms from printed pages
03-24-tear-sheets.md.figcaption: Tear sheets and mail-order catalogs trained buyers to decide from paper decades before lifestyle photography.

04-25-ebay-yahoo.md.alt: Vintage personal computer at a computer museum, stand-in for the first home-office online storefront era
04-25-ebay-yahoo.md.figcaption: eBay, Yahoo Stores, and early shop sites taught payments and photography before they solved furniture logistics.

04-26-photography-as-showroom.md.commons: Studio Lighting Equipment WMDE IMG 3277 edit.jpg
04-26-photography-as-showroom.md.alt: Studio lighting equipment aimed at a product set, when the photograph replaced the physical showroom
04-26-photography-as-showroom.md.figcaption: When the photograph became the showroom, shops began shaping objects for thumbnails, not for daylight in a dining room.

04-27-freight-is-not-shipping.md.alt: Semi-trailer truck on the road, typical LTL freight for bulky handmade furniture
04-27-freight-is-not-shipping.md.figcaption: Freight for furniture is dimensional weight, claims, and white-glove delivery—not the small-parcel logic of a cart checkout.

05-28-etsy-2005.md.alt: Brooklyn flea market stalls with vintage goods and handmade objects for sale
05-28-etsy-2005.md.figcaption: Etsy’s 2005 launch in Brooklyn rode the same handmade hunger visible in urban flea markets and craft booths.

05-29-jewelry-economics.md.commons: DFC 4162 A bustling outdoor market stall displays an array of handcrafted metal trinkets and keepsakes as a shopper examines items under soft evening lights.jpg
05-29-jewelry-economics.md.alt: Outdoor market stall selling small handcrafted metal goods while a shopper browses in evening light
05-29-jewelry-economics.md.figcaption: Marketplaces tuned for jewelry economics—small parcels, fast turns—strain furniture makers built for slow wood.

05-30-handmade-wars.md.commons: Display of handmade pottery and wooden items in a craft market.jpg
05-30-handmade-wars.md.alt: Handmade pottery and wooden craft items crowded on a market table
05-30-handmade-wars.md.figcaption: Etsy’s handmade policy fights were really fights over factory help, disclosure, and who gets to use the word artisan.

05-31-three-buckets.md.alt: Antique wooden furniture grouped in a vintage resale setting
05-31-three-buckets.md.figcaption: Etsy’s vintage, supplies, and handmade buckets let one storefront sell three different contracts under one brand.

05-32-fees-and-ads.md.commons: Old cash register 金銭登録機(きんせんとうろくき).jpg
05-32-fees-and-ads.md.alt: Vintage shop cash register on a retail counter
05-32-fees-and-ads.md.figcaption: Listing fees, payment processing, and off-site ads are the hidden rent in a marketplace that calls itself community.

05-33-etsy-wholesale.md.alt: Historic wholesale import company storefront, a brick retail door online wholesale programs tried to reach
05-33-etsy-wholesale.md.figcaption: Etsy Wholesale tried to bridge online makers and brick retailers—a different door than the consumer cart.

06-34-overstock-partners.md.commons: BLM Regional Seed Warehouse, Boise, ID (27159148551).jpg
06-34-overstock-partners.md.alt: Regional warehouse shelving stacked with palletized inventory awaiting partner fulfillment
06-34-overstock-partners.md.figcaption: Overstock’s partner model grew by listing other people’s inventory before owned closeouts dominated the story.

06-35-csn-wayfair.md.commons: Galveston, Houston & Henderson (GH&H) Freight Depot -- Galveston.jpg
06-35-csn-wayfair.md.alt: Historic Galveston freight depot where railroad logistics moved goods toward distant retail catalogs
06-35-csn-wayfair.md.figcaption: CSN Stores’ niche sites foreshadowed Wayfair: supplier-direct catalogs scaled by SEO and dropship logistics.

06-36-dropship-job.md.alt: Accordion conveyor moving cartons through a warehouse packing line
06-36-dropship-job.md.figcaption: Dropship assigns the website the relationship while the shop still builds, packs, and answers for the object.

06-37-high-point-recruitment.md.alt: Large trade exhibition hall aisle with vendor booths and hanging signs
06-37-high-point-recruitment.md.figcaption: Platform buyers walked High Point like traditional retailers, asking family shops for catalogs to digitize.

06-38-sku-flood.md.alt: Handheld barcode scanner reading a package label in a fulfillment operation
06-38-sku-flood.md.figcaption: SKU floods flatten a bench-made table into one row among thousands of look-alike listings.

06-39-map-private-label.md.commons: 1972 Buick Centurion, Original Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price window sticker, buick-centurion-sticker.jpg
06-39-map-private-label.md.alt: Manufacturer’s suggested retail price window sticker showing published list pricing rules
06-39-map-private-label.md.figcaption: MAP policies and private-label lines are how platforms and brands negotiate who controls the public price.

06-40-returns-chargebacks.md.commons: EFTA00002256 - Stacked cardboard boxes fill the corner of a warehouse room with white doors and an exit sign above.jpg
06-40-returns-chargebacks.md.alt: Stacked returned shipping cartons filling a warehouse corner near an exit sign
06-40-returns-chargebacks.md.figcaption: Furniture return rates and card chargebacks punish shops when photographs promised a room the object cannot enter.

06-41-walking-away.md.alt: Closed retail shop front with shutters drawn down
06-41-walking-away.md.figcaption: Walking away from a platform pipe should finish open orders first—then reclaim photographs and specifications.

07-42-four-prices.md.commons: Furnished Room, New England Furniture & Carpet Co. - DPLA - d93153dc1018aec4818900cddd84b1f2.jpg
07-42-four-prices.md.alt: Historic furnished room display from New England Furniture and Carpet Company retail photography
07-42-four-prices.md.figcaption: The same oak can carry four prices depending on door: gallery, wholesale, trade, or dropship markup.

07-43-american-made.md.alt: Made in USA country-of-origin label sewn onto product packaging
07-43-american-made.md.figcaption: American made shifted from shop-floor fact to marketing copy as imports and platforms scaled.

07-44-series-close.md.commons: Woodworking Tools at the Women's Woodshop in Minneapolis, MN.jpg
07-44-series-close.md.alt: Woodworking tools on a bench at the Women's Woodshop in Minneapolis, Minnesota
07-44-series-close.md.figcaption: The series closes back on the bench: touch the wood, ask which retail door you are standing in, and keep the words honest.
